descriptions.text: Eighth Floor Book of Lore – (Random starting location. Full title will reveal itself upon purchase)

recap.text: At thirty hands, Carl buys the Eighth Floor boon from Chaco's case, where the only other item, a checkered flag, has already sold to Prepotente. In the seventh floor's starting chamber, Carl pulls out a thin hardback titled Commonwealth of the Bahamas, which falls open on an owl creature called the Chickcharney. With twenty seconds left, Carl tells Donut to pick the Bahamas; she spins to the Caribbean and clicks, and Carl cries that it wasn't the Bahamas.

Donut explains that as party leader she picked a place close, and Carl decides she was wrong: the Bahamas book is a trap. He finds Shi Maria, a screaming spider woman who needs moisturizer, among the unique monsters in its index. At Donut's insistence he reads the book to lonely Prepotente for an hour, and the goat only points out typos. Mongo chomps La Ciguapa asleep, and she drops two cards.

beats.headline: Thirty hands, one each
beats.text: At thirty hands, Chaco's prize case has only two items, both Future Floor Boons, with a sign under them: limited to one each. One is a little checkered flag, Seventh Floor Pole Position, already sold out. Prepotente bought it, Chaco says; he was the first customer. The other is an Eighth Floor Book of Lore, its starting location random and its full title to be revealed upon purchase. Carl takes it, along with the shrink wand, the Skedaddle sheet music, a case of twenty-four Feather Fall potions and a case of healing potions.
beats.gist: At thirty hands, Carl buys Chaco's last Future Floor Boon, an Eighth Floor Book of Lore.

beats.headline: Book of Lore – Something
beats.text: In the seventh floor's starting chamber, Prepotente wants the full title of the eighth-floor boon. Carl makes him explain what he is doing first, and the goat asks again: please, tell me its name. Carl pulls out a thin hardback, Book of Lore – Commonwealth of the Bahamas, with the aquamarine and gold stripes and black triangle of the Bahamas flag on its cover and nothing else. Inside are descriptions and stats of monsters, and it falls open on an owl creature called the Chickcharney. The Bahamas? Donut says. That's where Miss Beatrice went for her vacation.
beats.gist: Donut and Carl hand Prepotente a thin Bahamas-flag Book of Lore, which opens on the Chickcharney owl creature.

beats.headline: Twenty seconds at the globe
beats.text: Squad Leader Donut must spin a holographic globe and choose the eighth floor's starting location, and Carl has told nobody but Prepotente what his lore book covers. If the pole position boon is anything to go by, he tells her, the Bahamas book was designed to be really helpful, though he kind of wants the western United States, which they know. Donut wants Ibiza. With twenty seconds left Carl says go with the Bahamas: they have the lore book. Donut agrees, insists they are absolutely not going into the water this time, spins to the Caribbean and clicks. Goddamnit, Donut, Carl cries. That wasn't the Bahamas.
beats.gist: Donut spins to the Caribbean with twenty seconds left, and Carl cries that it isn't the Bahamas.

beats.headline: Somewhere close, obviously
beats.text: Throwing themselves right into the Bahamas was a bad idea, Donut explains in the empty hall, so as party leader she picked somewhere close. They gave Carl a book about the place Miss Beatrice was: it was quite obviously a trap. Its usefulness is painfully obvious, and Carl understands her logic, but she was wrong. Bea and her friends flew there on the twenty-sixth, after phase one would have moved them on, so they would never have seen their ghosts there; with a second location for phase two, the show has plenty of time to engineer a scene with her. Then Donut reports that Prepotente is in the Bahamas.
beats.gist: Donut picked a nearby spot as party leader, and it was a trap; Prepotente is there.

beats.headline: The index at the back
beats.text: Sister Ines's people lost a flag trying to tag one of the local mobs, and Carl pulls the Bahamas book out and flips to the index for the first time. Prepotente seemed to think there would be some overlap. There are a lot of ridiculous monsters listed, mixed in with some that sound terrifying, sorted as Common, Uncommon, Rare, Very Rare, Legendary, Mythic and Unique. There are lots of birds and bats and fish. He sees no monk seal listed. He puts it away to examine more closely another time.
beats.gist: Carl pulls the Bahamas book's index, sorted Common to Unique, and finds no monk seal listed.

beats.headline: Among the unique monsters
beats.text: Samantha's messages describe a spider lady she calls Shi Maria, who says she is looking for her husband and has fangs with a very lovely shimmer. Carl pulls out the Bahamas book, turns to the index and finds Shi Maria listed in a sub-index as one of a monster's alternate names, in the very last section, under unique monsters. He turns it to show Donut and Mordecai. Donut peers at the image of the screaming spider woman: that lady really needs moisturizer.
beats.gist: Carl shows Donut and Mordecai Shi Maria's listing under unique monsters in the Bahamas book.

beats.headline: Just him and Bianca
beats.text: Donut has news from Prepotente: he wants Carl to read him a few chapters of that Bahamas book. He is all by himself there, and she thinks he is really lonely. He is not a member of any guild or the Desperado Club, and he is not allowed into Club Vanquisher anymore, so it is just him and Bianca, who is really nice but does not talk. They are moving toward Samantha, Carl answers, but it will be a few days before they get there; he will talk to Pony after.
beats.gist: Donut says Prepotente is lonely and wants Carl to read him chapters; Carl says in a few days.

beats.headline: An hour read to Pony
beats.text: On Donut's insistence, Carl spends a good hour reading directly from his Bahamas book and transcribing it into his notepad, copying it to the cookbook and to Prepotente in chat at the same time. The goat does not even thank him. He only answers when Carl asks whether the messages are arriving, and then only to point out a few typos in his translation.
beats.gist: Carl spends an hour transcribing his Bahamas book for Prepotente, who thanks no one and only corrects typos.

beats.headline: La Ciguapa, asleep
beats.text: Mongo chomps to death a hairy woman with backward feet, asleep under a pile of foliage, before she fully wakes. She is La Ciguapa, and there is an entry on her in the Bahamas book: she lures opponents with charm and is hard to kill, except by familiars and pets. She is Legendary, so another is unlikely, which makes her a wasted opportunity for the deck. The good news is that she drops two cards.
beats.gist: Mongo chomps La Ciguapa, a hairy woman with backward feet, to death asleep, and she drops two cards.

relations.note: Carl reads it to him in chat
